messages:
sam_dev: Hey all — onboarding hit a weird fail. Running the sample node app from the repo behind our corporate proxy + Okta SSO and the first API call returns 403. Body says "billing_required" but I think it might be an auth header strip. Anyone seen this?

maria_dx: can you paste the curl -v output? also are you using a service key or the token copied from the web session? web tokens don't always work for API calls.

sam_dev: here's the curl output (redacted ids):

```
> curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
* Connected to api.redwood.example (10.0.0.1) port 443 (#0)
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.example
> Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
> User-Agent: curl/7.68.0
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
< Content-Type: application/json
< x-request-id: 01H3Z7XXXX
< Content-Length: 92
<
{"error":"billing_required","message":"workspace not active or missing billing info"}
```

sam_dev: i'm 99% sure the token is from the browser after an okta redirect — not a service key. also we route through a corporate proxy so headers might be getting dropped.

tony_se: two likely issues: 1) the browser session token is ephemeral and tied to cookies/redirects — not meant for server API calls; 2) corporate proxies sometimes rewrite/remove Authorization. check your env for HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY and try unsetting them for a quick test, or add the API host to NO_PROXY.

tony_se: quick test you can run locally: `HTTP_PROXY= HTTPS_PROXY= curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer <SERVICE_KEY>\" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate` — if that works, proxy was the culprit.

sam_dev: ok how do i get a service key? i can’t find the option in the console (tenant's billing might be in a weird state).

maria_dx: flow in the console -> Settings -> Service keys. Create a new service key (name it e.g. sample-app-dev). Copy the value and set env `REDWOOD_API_KEY` or `REDWOOD_SERVICE_KEY` depending on sample. If billing is not enabled for the workspace you'll still see the billing_required error; open the Billing tab and verify status (or apply the free onboarding credits we email new orgs).

maria_dx: also add `NO_PROXY=api.redwood.example` if your proxy is the issue. for node samples, the env var to pick up is `process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY` — confirm the sample isn't reading `REDWOOD_TOKEN` from local storage.

sam_dev: tried creating a service key and re-running with proxies unset. success! got 200 and a short model output. pasted the curl success snippet:

```
> curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_12345" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
{"id":"resp_01H3Z8","object":"generation","choices":[{"text":"Hello from Redwood!","index":0}],"model":"rw-1-small"}
```

sam_dev: :raised_hands: looks like the combination of using the browser token + proxy was the root cause. billing page ended up being a red herring (workspace had no billing method, but service key + trial credits resolved).

onboarding-bot: Tip: see onboarding runbook -> https://redwood.internal/runbooks/onboarding-proxy-okta for proxy/okta troubleshooting and how to create service keys.

maria_dx: can someone add a short note to the sample-app README about SSO tokens vs service keys and proxy NO_PROXY examples? saved me a support ping later.

sam_dev: will send a PR to sample-app README with the exact env var examples and a note about Okta session tokens.

maria_dx: thanks — marking this resolved.
